title: Leverage over Z-Sums (Fantasy Basketball, H2H category)
body: CONCEPT: Leverage over Z-Sums. SPORT: Fantasy Basketball (Yahoo H2H category auction). WHAT IT MEASURES: A player's value as how much he raises your WIN-PROBABILITY in categories you can actually win this matchup, not his summed category z-scores. HOW TO READ IT: High leverage = he moves a live category; a stat-stuffer in a category you've already locked or already lost has low leverage even if his z-total is huge. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: The core of category drafting; beats z-sum / total-value rankings that over-pay for production in categories that don't change a matchup. COMMON MISTAKE: Chasing raw z-totals regardless of which categories are still in play. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).

title: Emergent Punts (Fantasy Basketball, H2H category)
body: CONCEPT: Emergent Punts. SPORT: Fantasy Basketball (H2H category). WHAT IT MEASURES: Which categories you punt, treated as something that EMERGES from the rosters actually achievable given the player pool, your budget, and draft state -- not a plan declared before the draft. HOW TO READ IT: Your punts reveal themselves as you build; a 'pure' single-category punt often collapses into a multi-category punt or the balanced build because the pool lacks cheap-but-elite-elsewhere players to realize it. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Category roster construction; beats declare-a-punt-then-force-it, which fights the pool. COMMON MISTAKE: Locking a punt up front before pool and state support it. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).

title: Build Identity / Archetype Fit (Fantasy Basketball)
body: CONCEPT: Build Identity (Archetype Fit). SPORT: Fantasy Basketball (H2H category). WHAT IT MEASURES: How strongly a player anchors a particular build (e.g. a punt-FT% big, a guard stack), from his per-category profile against the archetype's category emphases. HOW TO READ IT: ANTI-fitting players identify a build more strongly than weak fits -- a low-FT% center signals punt-FT% intent harder than a generically good player signals anything. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Reading which build a player commits you toward; beats treating every player as build-neutral value. COMMON MISTAKE: Scoring a player as build-agnostic when his weaknesses actually define a build. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).

title: Bayesian Competitor Inference (Fantasy Basketball)
body: CONCEPT: Bayesian Competitor Inference. SPORT: Fantasy Basketball (H2H category auction). WHAT IT MEASURES: A running posterior over which build each opponent is pursuing, updated from the players they buy and the prices they pay. INPUTS (general): opponents' acquired players, per-build likelihoods, purchase prices. HOW TO READ IT: It tells you who is contesting the categories and players you want, so you know where prices will rise. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Live auction bidding; beats static ADP / preseason ranks that ignore who is actually in the room. COMMON MISTAKE: Bidding to your private value while ignoring opponent state. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).

title: League-Demand Inflation (Fantasy Basketball auction)
body: CONCEPT: League-Demand Inflation. SPORT: Fantasy Basketball (H2H category auction). WHAT IT MEASURES: How much a candidate's expected price is inflated when several opponents' builds all value him strongly (an inflation factor). HOW TO READ IT: A (+%) on a player means contested demand -- pay up or pivot; a flat factor means you can buy near natural value. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Setting how aggressive to be on a target; beats bidding to your own private valuation as if the room weren't bidding too. COMMON MISTAKE: Ignoring concentrated demand and getting priced out late. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).

title: Threat-Pressure Max-Bid (Fantasy Basketball auction)
body: CONCEPT: Threat-Pressure Max-Bid. SPORT: Fantasy Basketball (H2H category auction). WHAT IT MEASURES: How high your max bid should lift on a player you fit -- toward the top competing threat plus a fit premium -- when opponents would contest him, and stays at a stretch baseline when they wouldn't. HOW TO READ IT: The number tells you how far to chase before walking away. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Deciding when to keep bidding; beats a flat max-bid that ignores who else wants the player. COMMON MISTAKE: Using one max-bid regardless of whether anyone is pushing the price. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).

title: Structural Variance (Fantasy Basketball projections)
body: CONCEPT: Structural Variance. SPORT: Fantasy Basketball. WHAT IT MEASURES: Per-player projection uncertainty driven by player situation -- experience, role stability, injury, age -- rather than a flat percentage for everyone. HOW TO READ IT: A traded rookie coming off injury carries far wider bands than a stable veteran; high-variance purchases inform competitor inference less because they're noisier signals. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Weighting how confidently to act on a projection; beats flat-rate variance, which treats every projection as equally certain and erases the Jokic-vs-volatile-rookie distinction. COMMON MISTAKE: Treating all projections as equally trustworthy. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).

title: Ensemble Projection Blend (Fantasy Basketball)
body: CONCEPT: Ensemble Projection Blend. SPORT: Fantasy Basketball. WHAT IT MEASURES: A blended per-category projection from multiple public sources, each weighted by its audited per-category accuracy, with inter-source disagreement folded into the uncertainty. HOW TO READ IT: When sources agree the band is tight; when they disagree (a role-shift or rookie case) the band widens honestly. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: The projection layer everything else reads; beats trusting any single source, which carries that source's blind spots. COMMON MISTAKE: Picking one favorite source and ignoring how much the others diverge. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).

title: Achievability Conditioning (Fantasy Basketball)
body: CONCEPT: Achievability Conditioning. SPORT: Fantasy Basketball (H2H category). WHAT IT MEASURES: Win-probability targets conditioned on what is still ACHIEVABLE given your current roster, budget, and remaining pool -- not on an idealized full-strength team. HOW TO READ IT: If a category is no longer winnable, stop spending toward it and redirect to live categories. WHEN/BEATS: Mid-and-late draft target-setting; beats targeting categories in the abstract regardless of whether your team can still reach them. COMMON MISTAKE: Chasing a category you have already been locked out of. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).

title: Bluff-Catch (Fantasy Basketball auction)
body: CONCEPT: Bluff-Catch. SPORT: Fantasy Basketball (H2H category auction). WHAT IT MEASURES: Whether a contesting bid is a genuine threat or an opponent inflating the price to drain your budget, and when to call versus fold. HOW TO READ IT: A flagged bluff means the contester's build doesn't actually value the player -- you can let it go or make them pay. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Contested live bids; beats taking every competing bid at face value. COMMON MISTAKE: Always assuming a rival bid reflects real demand. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).

title: Slot Accountancy (Fantasy Basketball roster legality)
body: CONCEPT: Slot Accountancy. SPORT: Fantasy Basketball. WHAT IT MEASURES: Whether adding a player yields a LEGAL roster, decided by bipartite matching of players to position slots rather than greedy assignment. HOW TO READ IT: An addition that looks blocked may actually be legal -- a dual-eligible player already rostered can shift to free the slot via an augmenting path. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Any 'can I add this player' check; beats greedy slot-filling, which wrongly blocks legal rosters when a dual-eligible player holds a slot another candidate needs. COMMON MISTAKE: Calling a roster illegal because a greedy pass couldn't place everyone. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).

title: Mean Delta Matchup-Win (Fantasy Basketball)
body: CONCEPT: Mean Delta Matchup-Win. SPORT: Fantasy Basketball (H2H category). WHAT IT MEASURES: A player's value as the average change in your matchup-win probability he provides, capturing opportunity cost beyond which build he anchors. HOW TO READ IT: Pair it with build identity -- identity tells you WHICH build a player commits you to, mean-delta tells you HOW MUCH he actually moves your wins. WHEN TO USE IT / WHAT IT BEATS: Comparing two players for the same slot; beats using build identity alone, which says what kind of player but not how valuable. COMMON MISTAKE: Reading identity without the magnitude of win-probability change. SOURCE: Resolve internal / Wonka Resolve (concept only).
